Definition: Authoritative fail-closed governance gate for Type 2 subagent delegation, called by the bridge/Agent hook before SDK subagent execution.
Backend feature slice bridging Chirality fail-closed subagent governance to SDK-backed subagent execution with allowlists, sealed context, approval refs, and restricted child tools/cwd.
Pre-execution guard on the SDK Agent tool that invokes the bridge and fails closed before SDK subagent execution.
Type 2 task-agent context limited to folder contents and declared references, excluding undeclared ghost inputs.
Inputs not present in the sealed brief or declared sources, which must not be used during execution.
Non-empty human/gate evidence string traceable to approval; absent, ambiguous, mutable, or SDK-only data is treated as denial or human-ruling-needed.
Default-deny posture: missing, malformed, unknown, or error states result in denial or human-ruling-needed rather than permitted execution.
Set of candidate agents permitted for delegation; a non-allowlisted candidate is denied.
An eligible delegation candidate explicitly marked AGENT_TYPE: 2 with task-agent metadata; non-Type-2 candidates are denied.
Explicit narrow tool list and bounded working directory applied to child subagents; children must not inherit or expand parent capabilities.
SDK agents definitions generated or selected only from allowed Type 2 task-agent instructions with deterministic restricted tools and cwd.
TBD serialized decision object preserving product-owned semantics: decision behavior, denial reason, decision source, approval reference, candidate/scope facts, and DEL-08-05 handoff.
Audit-suitable reason code and summary using stable vocabulary, free of sensitive prompt or environment data.
Interface exposing child lifecycle metadata and output artifact-path hooks to DEL-08-05 without DEL-08-04 owning persistence.
An SDK tool-allow field that alone is not a restriction boundary; real restriction requires disallowed tools, permission mode, hooks, and overlay policy.
